relevance_note: Case report of four individually described HA20 patients from two Chinese families: "WES revealed heterozygous c.559C > T in the TNFAIP3 gene in P1, P2 and P3, while the c.259C > T mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene was identified in P4."
method_note:
I read the whole paper by hand and typed every value into a Python builder script in my scratch directory. No table was transcribed automatically. The script finds each quoted span in the paper with whitespace-, apostrophe- and dash-tolerant matching and copies the exact paper text, which keeps the thin spaces (U+2009) in variant strings, ages and units. It then checks that every span is verbatim, that every row has every field, and that each person has 20 checklist rows.

TABLES. Table 1 (patients as rows) supplied age at onset and 'Current age', recorded as age at last evaluation. Table 2 (patients as rows): its 'No' cells are the written word and are read as explicit absence, not as an undefined symbol. Table 3 has patients as columns. Its column headers are 'Case 1', 'Case 2' and 'Case 4' (Case n = Pn), each split into 'Pretherapy' and 'posttherapy'. Only pretherapy values were used. A laboratory feature was recorded as observed only when that value lies outside the table's 'Normal range' column, and the whole row is quoted so the normal range is visible. Table 3 '–' cells were not used to exclude anything, because no legend defines the symbol.

SCOPE. In scope are the four patients P1–P4, plus P4's two parents, who tested negative ('the mutation was not found in her parents'). The parents are labelled 'father of P4' and 'mother of P4' after the Fig. 3 legend ('F: father; M: mother'). The 'other members in family 1' who tested negative got no rows, because the text never says who they are or how many (the Fig. 1 pedigree is not in the file). No variants in other genes were found ('No mutations were detected in other genes associated with autoinflammatory diseases'). 'it was reported by other study [16]' refers to the c.559C > T variant, not to the same patients, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = false.

CONTRADICTIONS IN THE PAPER.
(1) P4 oral ulcers: the text says she had them ('due to oral ulcers, cough') but Table 2 gives Ulcers 'No'. Both rows were emitted and the checklist oral-ulcers item is 'not reported'. Genital ulcers were also left 'not reported' for P4, because that table cell is contradicted.
(2) The Fig. 2 legend gives knee synovitis (e) and ILD (f) to P3, but the case text cites Fig. 2e and 2f for P4, and Table 2 gives P3 lung 'No'. Both P3 rows were emitted, alongside the Table 2 lung 'No' row, and P3's checklist ILD item is 'not reported'.
(3) P1: Table 3 shows anti-dsDNA '+' before therapy, but the text says 'ANA and SSA were positive, while other autoantibodies were negative'.
(4) P4: she was referred with 'positive ANA and anti-ds DNA antibodies', but on admission 'no other autoantibody was detected', and Table 3 shows anti-dsDNA '–'.
(5) Ages: P4 is a '9-year-old girl' in the text but has a current age of 8.3 years in Table 1. Onset differs too: P4 'at the age of 7 years' vs 6.9 years in Table 1, and P2 'at age 2.6' vs 2.5 years. Table 1 values were used for the individuals table.
(6) Current treatment: for P2 the text gives etanercept, Etiasa and MTX, while Table 1 adds prednisolone. For P4 the text gives etanercept with low-dose prednisolone, while Table 1 adds CSA and diclofenac.
(7) P4: Table 2 gives Liver 'No' although ALT and AST were increased. Autoimmune hepatitis was kept 'excluded' on the strength of Table 2.

JUDGEMENT CALLS.
- P3 inheritance is recorded as 'de novo' because the authors say so ('de novo for P3'). Testing of his own parents is only implied (family-wide WES; 'not detected in other members in family 1'), not stated.
- 'Fever of unknown origin' (P2, P4) was not counted as recurrent fever. P1's 'intermittent fever for 6 months' was counted.
- P1's cytopenias were counted as autoimmune because of the positive Coombs test in the setting of SLE.
- P1's pericardial effusion and ascites were not counted as serositis.
- P3's anal fistula (archosyrinx) was not counted as GI ulcers or inflammation.
- P1's hypothyroidism was not counted as autoimmune thyroiditis.
- 'All patients had no signs of eye or skin problems' names the study's four patients, so it excludes eye and skin items for P1–P4 as a group statement. The paper itself contrasts P2's perianal abscess with this statement.
- P3's 'only had mild oral ulcers, arthralgia, and archosyrinx' was not used to exclude other features.
- P4 is_proband is null, because she is not called proband.
- P4's 'no family history of rheumatic diseases' was not applied to her parents' rows.
- No age at HA20 diagnosis is stated for anyone.
- Ages in ISO 8601 use decimal years where the paper gives decimals (e.g. P2.5Y).
